title: Most journey tests never run in CI and 20 of 51 fail on a clean local stack
steps: Start the local stack; cd frontend-next; E2E_CHROME_PATH=<chromium> npx playwright test --project=chromium
expected: Critical journeys (sign-up, sign-in, checkout) run on every PR and pass on a clean environment.
actual: CI runs only the messaging E2E workflow, and only when messaging files change. Locally: 29 passed, 20 failed, 2 skipped. With the tour disabled: 39 passed, 10 failed — 7 need a real Google client ID (not a product bug), 2 checkout tests create a product with no paid business (hidden by the current plan rule), 1 sign-up test uses a brittle CSS selector although the OTP screen appears. Messaging suite: 5/5 desktop, 5/5 phone.
impact: Journey regressions like F-001 (photo upload) and F-003 (delivery) reach production unnoticed.
fix: Fix the stale specs (dismiss or disable tours via storage state, give checkout a business with a plan fixture, replace the CSS selector with a role/text locator, mock or skip Google when no client ID). Add a blocking CI job that runs the chromium project against a Postgres service, as the backend job already does. Add this audit's order-journey and account-lifecycle scripts as specs.
